candidats.description: The Museum Brandhorst was opened in Munich on May 21, 2009. It displays about 200 exhibits from the collection of modern art of the heirs of the Henkel trust, Udo Fritz-Hermann and Anette Brandhorst. The building with its long, two-storey, rectangular structure and multi-coloured facade composed of 36,000 vertical ceramic louvres in 23 different coloured glazes was created by architects Sauerbruch Hutton and is located next to the Pinakothek der Moderne in the Kunstareal . The building has three exhibition areas which are connected by stairs.

candidats.description: This is the Center of Molecular Biosciences of the Karl-Franzens University of Graz, Austria. Designed by the german group of architects Seidel, Thoma, and Kummer, the center opened in 2007. The appearance of the buildings is dominated by adjustable vertical glass-louvres in front of an orange façade.

candidats.description: Karl-Franzens University of Graz, Austria. In 2004, the group of architects Seidel, Thoma, and Kummer (Ulm, Germany) was commissioned with the realization of the ZMB ("Zentrum für molekulare Biowissenschaften"). Construction started in 2005 and the center opened in 2007. The appearance of the buildings is dominated by adjustable vertical glass-louvres for sun-shading. On this day, however, the sun didn't shine and it was snowing heavily in Graz.
